subject: Renewal negotiation: bridge credit + variable-rate commit
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@slatehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Slate Health Procurement <procurement@slatehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity bump and renewal options

Hi Aditya,

Quick note from Slate after our Q4 usage spike — we need to increase committed throughput for our inference pipelines by ~35% starting Jan 15 to support a pilot across three new product lines.

We’re evaluating two pieces together: (1) a short-term bridge to cover Jan–Mar while our budget re-org finalizes, and (2) the renewal amendment for the rest of the year. Procurement asked me to get concrete options and any standard amendment language you can share so legal can start a review.

Key constraints:
- We need predictable per-token pricing to forecast Feb–Apr spend.
- Any bridge credit should be convertible to future committed capacity rather than a pure one-time credit if possible.
- SLA tier increase (lower P99 target) would help justify spend to our CTO — what would that cost delta look like?

Can you send 2–3 structured options (bridge credit + commit structure, or variable-rate commit) and an estimated timeline for signature and provisioning? We’d like to close this before the 1/10 internal budget freeze.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of Integrations
Slate Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@slatehealth.com>
Cc: Slate Health Procurement <procurement@slatehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Dec 2027 09:54:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity bump and renewal options

Thanks Ellen — appreciate the clear constraints. We can get this across the line quickly. High‑level options below; I attached a draft amendment (redwood_amendment_draft_v1.pdf) you can share with legal for redlines.

Option A — Bridge credit + mini-commit (fast provisioning)
- Immediate 35% capacity bump for Jan–Mar on existing model variant.
- Slate receives a bridge credit equal to 40% of Jan–Mar incremental spend; credit converts 1:1 to committed capacity if you annualize before Apr 1.
- No change to base per-token rate for the first three months; credits apply as invoice offsets.
- Provisioning target: 3 business days after signed amendment + payment authorization.
- SLA: temporary 99th percentile target of 1100ms (upgrade available for an incremental fee).

Option B — Variable-rate commit (predictable blended price)
- Create a variable commit band: commit to a blended monthly commit that flexs +/- 20% with true-up quarterly.
- Lower blended per-token price compared to on-demand; additional 12% discount on the marginal over-commit for the first quarter as an adoption incentive.
- Bridge credit available (20%) for any committed amount that is paid within 30 days.
- Provisioning target: 7 business days (requires capacity reservation).

Option C — SLA uplift + premium commit
- Move to SLAGold tier with tighter P99 and priority capacity for scheduled bursts.
- This would be a premium (listed as a multiplier on committed rates); we can run numbers once you confirm target P99 and burst profile.

Recommended next step: if procurement needs a legally clean short path, Option A gets you live fastest and keeps the credit conversion option you asked for. If Slate wants predictable blended economics through the year, Option B is the engineering-friendly long-term path.

I’ll loop in our finance and delivery leads internally to confirm margins and capacity availability. Do you want a brief 30‑minute call this week to pick a path?

—Aditya
Aditya Rao | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2027 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Slate Health — pricing ask (internal)

Team — quick internal. Slate needs to ship a 35% bump Jan 15 and wants bridge credit convertible into committed capacity. Procurement timeline: signature before 1/10 ideally (they said budget freeze but meant 1/10 — external said 1/10). My recommended commercial structure to balance speed and margin:

- Offer Option A (bridge credit + mini-commit) as primary: 40% bridge credit for Jan–Mar incremental spend, conversion 1:1 to committed capacity if they annualize by Apr 1.
- If they prefer longer-term predictability, fall back to Option B with a blended discount — proposal: 12% marginal discount for first quarter on over-commit and 8% recurring on blended commit.
- SLA uplift can be sold as an add-on at a 15% multiplier; I want legal to keep language simple so procurement can sign quickly.

Budget impact: finance says 40% credit is acceptable if we convert at current list rates (we keep margin if they convert to a larger commit). I need Kimberly to confirm the exact % discount we can give on the blended commit (I suggested 12% first-quarter marginal).

Kimberly — can you quick-ok the 12% marginal for the trial quarter and confirm if Po provisioning can be within 3 business days for the bridge? Marissa — if they sign A we should list this as a cross‑sell expansion play and book a follow-up EBR in Q2.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@slatehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Slate Health Procurement <procurement@slatehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 16:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity bump and renewal options

Aditya — thanks for the clear options and the draft amendment. Procurement reviewed and we’d like to proceed with Option A (bridge credit + mini-commit) with the conversion clause. Attached is our PO (Slate_PO_2027-12-20.pdf).

Small asks from legal/procurement:
- Can you confirm bridge credit language will say: "convertible to committed capacity at the same per-token rate as the bridge period"?
- We’ll need the amendment and final SOW signed by Dec 30 to meet internal approvals.

I attached the PO and a simple capacity forecast (slate_capacity_forecast.xlsx) so you can provision appropriately. Please route the amendment to our DocuSign link once you have final language.

Best,
Ellen

---
Attachment(s): Slate_PO_2027-12-20.pdf (application/pdf); slate_capacity_forecast.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
